sources.summary: Sustainability in architecture is often discussed as though it were a universal standard —and, in principle, it should be. Buildings are increasingly evaluated through energy performance, embodied carbon , certification systems, material efficiency , biodiversity, and whole-life impact. Yet the rules determining what must actually be done remain highly local. A project designed in London, New York, or Copenhagen may be shaped by stringent energy codes, environmental review, disclosure requirements, planning controls, and increasingly ambitious carbon targets . The same practice working elsewhere may encounter a very different regulatory landscape.
